title: dedicated-autoscaler-priority-burst-util-reporting-enhancement
author: Lina Ortega
description:
Motivation: Dedicated fleet autoscaler currently reports aggregate burst utilization and token-bucket metrics at the fleet level. When priority routing is enabled (e.g. high/standard/low priority tenants), the autoscaler can make suboptimal scale decisions because utilization and burst budgets are not attributed by priority. This leads to cases where low-priority sustained traffic starves high-priority burst capacity or where the fleet overscales to satisfy transient high-priority spikes.

What this PR does: Adds per-priority burst utilization reporting and smoothing, extends the token-bucket accounting to emit priority-tagged metrics, and surfaces per-priority throughput guarantees in the autoscaler decision pipeline. Changes are backward-compatible: if priority routing is not configured, metrics remain aggregated. Key pieces: 1) priority-tagged tokenbucket exporter (redwood/services/autoscaler/tokenbucket_exporter.py), 2) EWMA smoothing per priority in the autoscaler decision logic, 3) new metrics and Grafana dashboard panels, 4) API and config knobs for per-priority throughput_guarantee and burst_limits, and 5) integration + e2e tests.

Implementation notes: - Tokenbucket accounting now keeps a separate token state per priority key (derived from request route). We reuse the existing sharded stores to avoid global locks and emit metrics with label `priority=<high|standard|low>`. - Smoothing: use an EWMA with configurable alpha (default 0.2) per priority to prevent noisy spikes from triggering immediate scale-ups. - Decision logic: when evaluating scale-up/scale-down, the autoscaler now computes both fleet-wide and priority-weighted utilization and will prefer adding capacity if any priority with a throughput_guarantee is below its target and there is capacity headroom. Fallthrough behavior preserves current `throughput_guarantee=0` default. - Observability: emit `redwood.autoscaler.tokenbucket.tokens_available`, `...burst_utilization`, and `...smoothed_utilization` with priority labels and route hints. Add dashboards and alerts for priority imbalance.

Checklist: - [x] Tokenbucket per-priority accounting and metrics
- [x] EWMA smoothing and config knobs
- [x] Autoscaler decision integration and unit tests
- [x] Integration tests that simulate mixed-priority traffic patterns
- [x] Grafana dashboard + dashboard JSON export
- [x] Feature flag (rollout: `enable_priority_burst_reporting`)
- [x] Docs snippet and release notes

Backward compatibility and rollout: Default behavior unchanged. The feature is gated behind `enable_priority_burst_reporting=false` by default in infra. We will rollout to staging and then progressively to prod fleets. The metric names are additive; no breaking metric renames.

Related: Linear ENG-7421 (priority autoscaler improvements), ENG-7588 (obs: per-priority metrics), incident SUP-3102 (customer reported high-priority starve case).

review_conversation: Marco Rivera (2026-02-20): Requested change - can we avoid storing per-priority state in a single global map to reduce hot keys? Suggested sharded store; author replied they implemented a sharded tokenbucket store to avoid global locks.

Priya Patel (2026-02-22): Comment - please include a short note about the cost impact of extra metrics (cardinality). Lina replied that we reuse route hint labels only when enabled and the default config aggregates metrics; we also provide retention recommendations.

release_notes:
- Add per-priority burst utilization and tokenbucket metrics
- Autoscaler respects per-priority throughput guarantees when deciding scale operations
- Config knobs: enable_priority_burst_reporting, priority.ewma_alpha, priority.throughput_guarantee
- New Grafana dashboard panels and alerts for priority imbalance
summary: Adds per-priority burst reporting and smoothing to the dedicated autoscaler so throughput guarantees and priority routing are considered during scale decisions. Backward-compatible and gated behind a feature flag.
notes_for_ops: Feature is off by default. Staged rollout recommended: enable in staging -> 10% prod fleets -> 50% -> global. Watch metrics: redwood.autoscaler.smoothed_utilization{priority}, and alerts: autoscaler.priority_imbalance_high. If unexpected scale-ups observed, set enable_priority_burst_reporting=false and rollback.
tests: Unit: tokenbucket priority accounting, EWMA smoothing, decision heuristics. Integration: simulated mixed-priority traffic (high steady + standard burst + low background) verified target throughput_guarantees. E2E: dashboard panels validated in staging. CI: all tests passed on final run.
context: Customer impact: addresses cases where high-priority tenants experienced degraded burst capacity under mixed workloads (refer SUP-3102). Expected to reduce high-priority P99 latency regressions during mixed traffic spikes and avoid unnecessary fleet-wide scale-ups.
